title: How do two processes talk through a pipe?
question: /init makes a pipe and starts a child that runs cat, reading from it, as a shell does for `echo hello | cat`. What does the kernel do as one process waits for the other?
text: Call 1, [pipe2([8], 0)](1): [create_pipe_files](1:create_pipe_files) A pipe: a buffer in the kernel, and two files for it: fd 3 reads, fd 4 writes.

Call 2, [child = clone(CLONE_VM | CLONE_VFORK | SIGCHLD, 0, NULL, NULL, 0)](2): [copy_process](2:copy_process) A child process (vfork: no MMU, so it borrows /init's memory instead of copying it). It gets copies of /init's fds: the pipe's too. [wait_for_vfork_done](2:wait_for_vfork_done) Until the child runs a program of its own (or exits), /init waits: the call blocks.
Call 3, [child: dup3(3, 0, 0)](3): [do_dup2](3:do_dup2) The child's stdin (fd 0) is now the pipe's reading end: the same open file as its fd 3.
Call 4, [child: close(3)](4): [file_close_fd](4:file_close_fd) Its fd 3 is not needed any more: fd 0 has the pipe.
Call 5, [child: close(4)](5): [file_close_fd](5:file_close_fd) The child must not keep the writing end: else it would never see the end of the input.

Call 6, [child: execve("/bin/cat", {"cat", NULL}, NULL)](6): [begin_new_exec](6:begin_new_exec) The child runs cat: memory of its own now, its fds kept (fd 0: the pipe). cat reads its input: the pipe is empty, so it sleeps. [complete_vfork_done](6:complete_vfork_done) So /init need not wait any more: its clone returns the child's pid.
Call 7, [close(3)](7): [file_close_fd](7:file_close_fd) /init keeps the writing end only.

Call 8, [write(4, "hello\n", 6)](8): [anon_pipe_write](8:anon_pipe_write) Into the pipe's buffer... [try_to_wake_up](8:try_to_wake_up:any) ...and wake the reader: cat's read returns the 6 bytes, and it writes them to its output (the console).

Call 9, [close(4)](9): [pipe_release](9:pipe_release:any) No writer left: the pipe's readers are woken: cat's read returns 0, the end of its input, and it exits (SIGCHLD to its parent; a zombie until the parent asks how it ended).

Call 10, [waitid(P_PID, child, [128], WEXITED, NULL)](10): [do_wait](10:do_wait) How did the child end? (Its siginfo: it exited, status 0.) [wait_task_zombie](10:wait_task_zombie) The child is a zombie: its exit status is taken... [release_task](10:release_task) ...and it is reaped: the child is gone.
